📚 Today you learned

Net Revenue Retention (NRR)

Yesterday was ARR — the size of the recurring-revenue engine. NRR tells you whether that engine is getting bigger or leakier from the existing customer base alone, before counting a single new logo. Formula: (starting ARR + expansion − contraction − churn) ÷ starting ARR, measured over 12 months. 100% = a perfectly flat base. Above 110% is elite — the existing customers alone are growing revenue faster than most companies' entire top line. Below 100% means the bucket is leaking faster than it's being filled, no matter how flashy new-logo growth looks. Google Cloud's 82% revenue growth this quarter is mostly new workloads landing, but the NRR of its enterprise AI/cloud customers is the number that tells you if today's AI spend sticks around next year or churns to a cheaper competitor once contracts renew — a much better long-term signal than the headline growth rate.

Also today: Land-and-expand — a sales motion that starts with a small initial contract and grows the account over time; it's the mechanism that produces high NRR when it works.
